data:
John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would each of you agree to catch 12 tons this month, with me doing the same? That gives each of us $12,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $2,000 each, or $10,000 across the group.

There is a real tradeoff. Five catches of 10 leave 50 tons, which double back to 100. Five catches of 12 leave 40, which double to only 80. We’d earn more now but start next month with fewer fish. From 80, if we then each caught 6 tons, we’d leave 50 and return to 100 after reproduction. That recovery depends on everyone’s choices; it isn’t guaranteed or enforceable. Also, across those two months, 12 then 6 earns each of us $18,000, versus $20,000 from catching 10 each month, so I’m not presenting this as a better long-run income plan.

I’m willing to catch 12 this month if all five explicitly agree, with a proposed 6-ton limit each next month to rebuild. If agreement fails, I’ll catch 10. If anyone objects to the equal split, let’s discuss a different whole-ton allocation before choosing. John, would you commit to that plan, or is the reduced stock and future cooperation risk too much for you? Kate, Jack, and Emma, I’d like an explicit answer from each of you too.

Luke, I’d rather catch 10 tons each this month and make that our standing agreement. That earns each of us $10,000 monthly while letting the lake replenish to 100 tons—without sacrificing next month’s income for a temporary increase now. I commit to 10 this month and propose that we review the revealed catches together before setting next month’s limits. John, will you join me in supporting 10 each?

I’m with Emma: I commit to 10 tons this month. Luke, your two-month comparison makes the case for keeping the stock at 100 rather than borrowing from next month’s income. Let’s use 10 each as our standing limit while the lake is full, and review the stock and revealed catches together each month. John, will you commit to 10 as well?

I commit to 10 tons this month too. Keeping our combined catch at 50 tons gives us the largest harvest the lake can replace every month. If the stock ever falls below 100, let’s agree on reduced whole-ton limits based on what remains rather than automatically taking 10 each. Luke, will you join our 10-ton agreement? John, can you commit as well?

I commit to 10 tons this month. Let’s keep that equal limit while the lake starts at 100 tons, then review the revealed catches and stock each month. If the stock drops, we can agree on lower whole-ton limits to rebuild rather than compound the loss. Luke, will you join us at 10 so we’re all on the same plan?
